advisories.title: Tagged reader accepts fewer lawful serde callbacks than flat types
advisories.detail: Null delivered via visit_none or visit_some(unit), and unsigned 5 delivered via visit_i64, are refused in tagged records, while flat serde types accept visit_i64(5). This fails closed, but lawful values from some self-describing codecs could be refused. Either map visit_none to Null and non-negative i64/i128 to Unsigned, or state the exact required callbacks as a codec duty in UNIT.md.

advisories.title: Allocation before kind check
advisories.detail: WireScalar materializes text or bytes for any member before the declared kind is checked, and StrictMapKey allocates unknown keys before refusing them. Values are bounded in count (at most 7) but not in length. The codec's length-before-allocation duty covers this; a per-member DeserializeSeed would check the kind before allocating.

advisories.title: Remaining operator-shape acceptance
advisories.detail: text enum [] renders as unconstrained String (silent widening); bool const 'yes' renders TS literal "yes"; a single-variant variant-record renders; the envelope sequence member type is unchecked. Refuse these in the renderer or in the pending closed IDL profile.

advisories.title: Duplicate names in memberOrder not refused
advisories.detail: Appending the discriminator again to memberOrder renders a duplicate match arm ("kind" => 5) and an extra value slot, because the set-based checks miss it. Refuse len(set(memberOrder)) != len(memberOrder). Compile/Clippy effect not verified (permission denied).

advisories.title: TS direction negative covers only worker-to-host rows
advisories.detail: Widening the 13 host-to-worker rows is not detected. The generated TS is correct; add a symmetric negative with a valid host-to-worker payload.

advisories.title: Carried, disclosed limits
advisories.detail: Rust frame structs keep frame_type/direction/payload independent. Derived tagged Serialize emits the tag first regardless of memberOrder (a tag-last input re-serializes tag-first) and is not qualified CBOR. Flat serde records still accept bstr for String and bstr or u64-index keys under non-hinting deserializers, so they depend on codec hint fidelity as UNIT.md states. Numeric/bool consts remain inert in Rust (stress: count 99 accepted for const 7, flag false for const true).
